name: Teamleader Focus
subcategory: SMB CRM with quoting, invoicing and time tracking
tagline: All-in-one CRM, quotation, invoicing and time tracking tool aimed at small European service businesses.

pricing.basis: monthly per user, typically on top of a platform fee
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The visible surface of Teamleader is deceptively simple: contacts, deals, quotes, invoices, timesheets, a few dashboards. An agent will happily produce all of that in an afternoon and it will look fine. What it cannot produce is the boring half that makes the product legally usable: correct VAT handling across EU cases, structured e-invoicing into Peppol, payment reminders that hold up, and a working pipe into whatever software your accountant actually uses. Add multi-user access with an audit trail and you are building a small accounting vendor, not a weekend project. If you are a solo operator who only needs to remember who owes you what, the DIY version is genuinely fine; the moment a real bookkeeper or a tax authority is downstream, it is not.
coreLoopDIY: A local single-user app tracking companies, contacts, deals, quotes, invoices and logged hours, with printable PDF documents and CSV export for your accountant.
requirements: Node 20+ and a local machine or small VPS you are willing to back up
Your own VAT rates and invoice numbering rules entered by hand
A browser for print-to-PDF invoice output
Manual export to whatever your accountant wants
whatYouLose: Structured e-invoicing (Peppol and similar) and the VAT logic that keeps invoices compliant across EU cases
Direct integrations with accounting packages, banks and payment providers, so reconciliation becomes manual
Multi-user access, roles and an audit trail that a bookkeeper or auditor will accept
Mobile apps, email and calendar sync, and the small conveniences like quote follow-up and dunning sequences
Someone else's responsibility when invoice numbering, credit notes or tax rules go wrong
moatNotes: The interesting part is not the CRM, it is being plugged into the invoicing and accounting rails of a specific set of countries.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because invoicing is one of the few pieces of small business software where being wrong has a cost with a deadline attached. Teamleader sells a path from a deal in a pipeline to a compliant document in your accountant's inbox, and it keeps that path current as national e-invoicing rules change. Businesses also grow into it: two people can share a spreadsheet, five cannot, and the day you hire someone who needs to send quotes without touching your database, the DIY version quietly dies. The subscription is mostly paying someone to track regulation you do not want to read.
notes: The CRM half is a weekend of CRUD forms; the invoicing half is a compliance project with an audit at the end. The moat is being wired into European invoicing and accounting rails, plus the multi-user trail that makes those records defensible.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user freelance operations app called "Shopfront". No cloud, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript, server actions only, no separate API layer
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, Drizzle ORM, migrations checked into the repo
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost, database file at ./data/shopfront.db

Data model:
- Company: name, vatNumber, address, country, notes
- Contact: belongs to Company, name, email, phone, role
- Deal: title, company, value, currency, stage (lead, quoted, won, lost), expectedCloseDate, notes
- Quote: company, line items (description, qty, unitPrice, vatRate), validUntil, status (draft, sent, accepted, rejected)
- Invoice: company, line items, issueDate, dueDate, sequential number per year, status (draft, sent, paid, overdue), paidOn
- TimeEntry: date, minutes, description, optional deal link, billable flag, hourly rate

Features in scope:
- CRUD screens for every model, keyboard reachable, no modals for editing
- Kanban style deal board with drag between stages
- Convert an accepted quote into a draft invoice in one click, copying line items
- Invoice numbering strictly sequential per calendar year, enforced in a transaction, gaps impossible
- Printable invoice and quote pages at /print/invoice/[id] with clean print CSS so the browser produces the PDF; company details and logo path read from .env
- Dashboard: unpaid invoice total, overdue list, hours logged this week, open deal value
- CSV export for invoices, time entries and contacts, one file each
- Seed script with fake data

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt or fake:
- Peppol or any structured e-invoicing format
- Automated VAT determination: VAT rate is a manual field per line item
- Bank, payment provider or accounting software integrations
- Email sending, multi-user auth, roles, mobile app

Put business identity, default currency, default VAT rate and default hourly rate in .env with a .env.example. Add a README stating plainly that this is a personal record keeping tool, that invoice compliance is the operator's problem, and that data lives in one SQLite file that should be backed up.
